In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the theory of the source coding of information stable sources with finite alphabets and the channel coding of information stable channels with finite input and finite output alphabets.
the development of a theory for the computation of the optimistic capacity of arbitrary single-user systems.
the derivation and analysis of optimistic definitions of source and channel coding theorems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimistic definitions of the source and channel coding rates are more general than the conventional definitions, and that they provide a better characterization of the information content of a source or a channel.
the optimistic capacity is a better measure of channel capacity than is the conventional definition of capacity.
the conventional definitions are the best possible ones, and that the optimistic ones should not be used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimistic capacity of a channel equals the capacity of its dual channel.
the optimistic definitions of source and channel coding theorems are more general and flexible than their conventional definitions.
, for any single-user source or channel, we can find a reliable code for infinitely many block-lengths if we are willing to accept a rate which is slightly larger than the conventional rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for information stable channels, the optimistic capacity is equal to the conventional capacity.

the optimistic capacity of a channel can be significantly larger than its conventional capacity, and that this gap can be exploited in the design of efficient communication schemes for single-user channels.
the optimistic source coding theorems are not just a theoretical curiosity but can be used in the design of practical coding schemes.
